newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold eases, volume firms.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold eases, volume firms.

text.p: Traded volume on the Istanbul gold exchange rose to 909 kilos on Monday from Friday's 534 kilos as lower prices led banks to engage in arbitrage deals, as well as an increase in physical demand, dealers said.
Gold eased to $352.30 an ounce and 1,421,500 lira an ounce against $354.00 and 1,432,000 lira on Friday following lower levels on European markets.
"The lower prices encouraged some arbitrage dealing, but there was also some physical demand from the free market which pushed the day's volume up," one dealer said.
The Turkish lira edged higher to 125,300 lira to the dollar, versus 125,310 on Friday's close.
Most of the day's trade -- 512 kilos -- was registered in the morning session, with 77.8 percent of trade in lira terms. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875
